name: Hill View Restaurant
why_it_matters: Ranked #1 of Dhanaulti's three TripAdvisor-listed restaurants — a small balcony establishment opposite Hotel Drive Inn run by Yashpal Singh Belwal. Fresh parathas and rooftop pine-tree views are why Mussoorie-bound travellers stop here for breakfast.
insider_tip: The card machine has been unreliable for years per recent reviews — bring cash. Take the balcony seat over the indoor section for the Garhwal ridge view.
signature_address: Chamba Road, Opposite Hotel Drive Inn, Dhanaulti, Tehri Garhwal 249179

name: Midway Restaurant & Guest House
why_it_matters: A no-frills budget canteen on the highway with rooftop seating and ₹200 thalis. TripAdvisor lists it as #2 in Dhanaulti, but the appeal is volume and price, not refinement — this is where day-trippers from Mussoorie eat lunch.
insider_tip: Kitchen closes at 11pm, but tandoor goes off at 9:30pm. Order the chowmein-tandoori combo if travelling with kids — it's the only menu sweet spot for fussy eaters.

name: Meal on Hill Cafe & Restaurant
why_it_matters: A small ridge cafe on the Chamba-Mussoorie road overlooking Tehri's oak slope. Standard hill-station menu (paratha, maggi, chai) with the view doing the heavy lifting. Closes at 10pm sharp.
insider_tip: The window-bench seats face the valley — ask for those instead of the parking-side tables. Service slows after 7pm when the kitchen runs lean.

name: Highlander's Cafe & Stay
why_it_matters: A small rooftop cafe attached to a guesthouse — the closest thing Dhanaulti has to a young-traveller cafe in the Old Manali / Kasol mould. Continental and Chinese skew on the menu; popular with weekending Delhi backpackers.
insider_tip: Open till 11pm — one of the few places in town that serves dinner past 10. The Continental items are hit-or-miss; stick to the Chinese wok dishes which the kitchen does cleanly.
signature_address: Dhanaulti Road, near main market, Dhanaulti, Tehri Garhwal 249179

name: Glass House Restaurant (Apple Orchard Resort)
why_it_matters: A glass-walled dining structure cantilevered over the cliff at Apple Orchard Resort, 2km from Dhanaulti's centre on the Kanatal road. The most photographed dining room in Dhanaulti; the buffet leans on apples grown on the property.
insider_tip: Non-resident diners need to call ahead — the restaurant prioritises in-house guests at peak hours. The breakfast buffet is open from 7-10am and is better value than the à la carte dinner.
signature_address: Apple Orchard Resort, Bhandari Gaon, Dhanaulti, Tehri Garhwal 249179

name: Eco Park Snack Stalls (Amber & Khumber)
why_it_matters: The cluster of small canteens and food carts outside Amber & Khumber Eco Parks — Dhanaulti's two flagship picnic spots. Chai for ₹20, plate of maggi for ₹50; this is what most day-trippers actually eat between deodar walks.
insider_tip: No food is sold inside the parks — eat before entering or at the carts opposite the gate. Cash only at most stalls; the bhutta vendor at the parking lot does the freshest sweet corn (October-March).
signature_address: Amber & Khumber Eco Parks, Mussoorie-Chamba Road, Dhanaulti, Tehri Garhwal 249179

name: Kaddukhal Trail-Head Dhabas
why_it_matters: The cluster of family-run dhabas at Kaddukhal — the road-head village where the 1.5km Surkanda Devi temple trek begins, 6.7km from Dhanaulti. Pilgrims eat here before and after the climb; mandua (finger millet) roti and rajma are the local staples.
insider_tip: Eat AFTER the trek, not before — the climb is steep enough that a heavy paratha will slow you down. Most dhabas pack a thali for ₹150-200 by 8am for early-morning pilgrims.
signature_address: Kaddukhal village, Mussoorie-Chamba Road, Saklana Range, Tehri Garhwal 249179
